brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.

requirements.requirement: Keep sewing supplies tidy - compartmentalized storage
requirements.evidence: 3 cells with bins: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments), bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments), bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full (large open). Provides separated compartments for small notions like buttons, needles, bobbins and larger space for fabric/scissors. End caps and joint bolts secure build.

requirements.requirement: Ability to hold / display sewing accessories (e.g., tape, small items, spool area)
requirements.evidence: Props placed: prop:1 tape-gaffer, prop:2 tape-electrical, prop:3 heap-screws-div2 as stand-in for buttons/notions - shows compartment use. Two rod sockets (accessory:0#0,0#1, accessory:0#0,0#2) provide potential spool/ribbon holders. No dedicated sewing-specific props in catalog, so generic small-item props demonstrate intent.

finish.summary: Compact 3-cell sewing caddy: two divided bins for small haberdashery and one deep open bin for fabric/tools, with capped faces and locked joints. Dressed with tapes and button-like heaps to show tidy compartment use; two rod accessories offer vertical spool/ribbon mounting points.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
